extracted.intended_audience: general readers; prospective authors, researchers, and students interested in the Yale Journal on Regulation
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia entry summarizing the Yale Journal on Regulation: its history, scope, publication details, notable alumni, and a named prize. Useful for readers seeking descriptive information about the journal and high-level guidance on its topical focus and submission types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / topical focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal publishes articles, essays, notes, and commentaries that cover a wide range of topics in regulatory, corporate, administrative, international, and comparative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the substantive subject areas the journal considers appropriate for submission; prospective authors should align manuscripts with these topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission types
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes articles, essays, notes, and commentaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the formats of work the journal runs (long-form articles, shorter essays/commentaries, and student notes), implying expectations about variety of length and treatment though no explicit length/format rules are given on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walton H. Hamilton Prize — award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Walton H. Hamilton Prize is awarded to the most outstanding accepted manuscript on the study and understanding of regulatory policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize signals a recognition criterion (outstanding contribution to the study/understanding of regulatory policy) for accepted manuscripts; authors working directly in regulatory-policy analysis may be especially competitive for this honor.
